# LLMLOCAL

well, i was intrigued by the idea of seeing the "thought process" of some local models that isn't visible in online LLMs.. While I'm not the biggest user of them, I have occasionally gotten useful code from chatgpt/claude

this is as hello world as possible.. the only features are
* hitting a gguf file
* some memory storage with some attempts at sentence-transformers

**This is a personal project to have some fun with local models; the rest of this readme was generated by claude code:**

One script, `llm.py`, and a small vector memory beside it in `llm/vector/`.

```sh
python llm.py "your message here"
python llm.py "remember this: I like concise answers"
```

A message is first matched against the memory (the five closest stored
sentences, embedded with `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5` through sentence-transformers,
CPU only, from the local cache) and then handed to a llama.cpp binary with the
GGUF model: 4096 context, up to 32768 tokens. Whatever the model prints,
thinking included, is printed as is. A message starting with `remember this:`
stores the rest instead of asking anything.

Before it runs, fill in the three empty paths at the top of `llm.py`
(`LLAMA_BIN`, `MODEL_PATH`, `VECTOR_DIR`) and install `torch` and
`sentence-transformers`. `llm/config.json` has slots for mistral, mixtral and
deepseek but nothing reads it yet; that is the one TODO. Models, the pickle
the memory lives in and anything secret are gitignored. No tests, no license.
